title: observability-target.v2
description: One inventory document. Either the scrape jobs for one product, or one federation import. The `kind` discriminator keeps the two apart: they render differently and rule 9 applies to only one of them.  Branching is if/then on `kind` rather than oneOf: oneOf collapses every branch's errors into one 'not valid under any of the given schemas', which tells an operator nothing about which field is wrong.  v2 applies ADR-0004. A job declares a LOGICAL `target_id` and whether it authenticates; it no longer carries `endpoints` or a `credential`, both of which moved to the private inventory. The one way an endpoint can still be written down here is inside a `publication` block that also demands a rationale — so the per-target exception is enforced by construction rather than by a check, because there is no field an endpoint can be typed into that does not also ask why publishing it is acceptable. The block carries no approver: the approval is the protected-branch merge that accepted the rationale, which is externally attested, and a name in the file would be a second and weaker claim about the same event.

publication.description: The ADR-0004 per-target exception: a deliberate decision to publish a resolved endpoint in public Git. Legitimate for a target already on the public internet, where indirection buys nothing. Both fields are required together, which is the whole design — an exception that could be taken by leaving a field out is the default this contract exists to remove.  It carries NO approver field, deliberately. A name typed into a tracked file is self-attested: nothing verifies it, the person named never sees it, and it manufactures the appearance of an approval record where there is none. What authorizes this disclosure is the protected-branch review that merged it, which is externally attested and carries immutable coordinates. The rationale is here because a reviewer must be able to disagree with it; the approval is in the merge, where it can be checked.

endpoints.description: Published deliberately. When present these are used INSTEAD of the private inventory's binding for this target_id, so the exception is also the resolution and the two can never disagree.

rationale.description: Why publishing this endpoint is acceptable. Minimum length is deliberate: 'already public' without saying how it is already public is an assertion, not a review.

owner.description: Accountable team or person for these targets. A target nobody owns is a target nobody restores.

target_id.description: The LOGICAL identity of what this job scrapes, for example `erp-production`. Resolved against the private inventory at promotion time, or against a `publication` block when one is declared. Distinct from `job`: the job name is what Prometheus labels the series with, the target_id is what the endpoint is looked up by, and conflating them would tie a rename of one to a rename of the other.

metrics_path.description: PUBLIC, settling one of the two classifications ADR-0004 left open. A path is scrape protocol rather than topology when it is the conventional one; a non-default value is topology wearing a protocol field's name, and must carry `path_rationale`.

path_rationale.description: Required when `metrics_path` is not `/metrics`. States why the non-default path is protocol rather than concealment — because a path chosen precisely because it is not guessable is a secret in a field the contract does not treat as one.

authenticated.description: Whether this job presents a credential. A CAPABILITY, which ADR-0004 publishes, as against the credential BINDING, which it does not. Resolution refuses a disagreement in either direction, so the public claim is falsifiable rather than decorative.

expected.description: How many targets this job MUST report as up. Live verification compares against this number, because a job that scrapes zero targets reports no failures. Checked against the resolved endpoint count, which is why the check now runs at resolution rather than over the public document alone.

target_id.description: The logical upstream. Its endpoint is a federation endpoint, which ADR-0004 lists as private without qualification.

rename_prefix.description: AGENTS.md rule 9. Imported `up` and `scrape_*` are renamed to <prefix>up etc. so a central rule can never mistake an upstream's health for a target this plane owns. Required: there is no correct federation without it.
